learner_operation: Identify pivot columns of an already row-echelon-form integer matrix by locating the first nonzero entry in each nonzero row.

fixed_features.feature: Already REF integer matrices of the observed small shapes
fixed_features.justification: The target KP and tutorial define pivots as leading nonzero entries; eliminating a general matrix belongs to later lesson steps. Shape profiles preserve visual workload.

fixed_features.feature: Nonempty pivot set in learner-facing checkbox practice
fixed_features.justification: All supplied checkbox sources contain pivots and require selecting columns. Excluding the zero matrix keeps this observed response contract; no observed source family is removed.

fixed_features.feature: Complete per-column checkbox bank or five-choice radio bank
fixed_features.justification: These are the two captured response contracts. Radio ranks 2 and 3 with equally sized candidate subsets give conservative same-method practice; not every mathematically possible rank is needed.

fixed_features.feature: Matrix names tied to source profiles
fixed_features.justification: A name is irrelevant to pivot membership. Controlled target changes and all visible shape/name cue groups contain differing answers, so no fixed name-to-answer assignment is supported.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Move leading positions while preserving increasing pivots and REF; each column may qualify or fail.
answer_roles.observed: 248 raw samples and 221 delivered samples retain 96 distinct shape/target cases. Leading, trailing, all-column and intermediate decisions occur; all 16 source profiles exercised. One metadata profile collapses to one record after content deduplication because another profile has identical visible wording/shape; the merged visible group remains varied.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Vary nonzero-row count at comparable easy workload.
answer_roles.observed: Ranks 1,2,3,4 observed in checkbox practice; radio ranks 2 and 3. Exact batch ranks 1,2,3 with five distinct shape/target cases.

answer_roles.role: Radio correct subset and choice position
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Derive bank and key from current leading positions, vary subset and position independently of matrix coefficients.

coverage.case: Original source profiles and both response contracts
coverage.result: 16/16 supported practice-source cases replay complete banks, keys, prompts and solutions. Canonical example has no captured answer controls; its displayed matrix is checked separately without claiming a missing bank was captured.

coverage.case: Relevant decisions before and after delivery
coverage.result: 248 -> 221 after 27 content duplicates; all 96 tested shape/target cases remain. Visible shape/name cue groups have multiple targets.

All 5 survive, including 3 checkbox and 2 radio records; ranks 1:2, 2:2, 3:1. Constant column 2 answers 2/3 checkbox records, nonzero-column heuristic 0/3, stored positions 3 and 5 answer one radio each. Tiny singleton cue lookups are not claimed to prove a generator-wide rule.

counterfactuals.change: Checkbox: set first row column 1 from 2 to 0; radio: set second row column 2 from 4 to 0. Keep other entries, seed, profile, response format and radio bank fixed.
counterfactuals.expected: Checkbox pivots change (1,3)->(2,3); radio pivots change (1,2,4)->(1,3,4). Before-response must fail the changed membership while the new response passes.
counterfactuals.observed: Prompts, column vectors, correct keys, named solution columns, solution matrices and rendered summaries change together. Native transferred old checkbox response is rejected on the two changed memberships; old radio subset is rejected. All newly correct choices pass.
counterfactuals.justification: The tutorial defines the first nonzero entry of each nonzero row as its pivot; moving it must move the qualifying column.

counterfactuals.change: Change a trailing entry: checkbox row1 col3 -1->8; radio row2 col5 3->-8. Preserve leading entries and bank.
counterfactuals.expected: Same pivot subsets and same accepted learner response, while prompt, vectors and worked-solution matrices show the changed entry.
counterfactuals.observed: Correct subsets preserved; all transferred before-responses accepted by native grader. Rendered summaries retain the same named columns and rendered matrices contain changed entries.
counterfactuals.justification: Entries to the right of a leading nonzero cannot change its position.

shortcut_probes.conclusion: Both preview fixtures show the correct option first. This is specific to fixture contentIds 3 and 4 with prepublication UUID field IDs; the actual UI hashes task-item and field entity IDs. On accepted records over item IDs 1..128, this strategy succeeds 46/256 versus the 1/5 baseline. The preview coincidence does not demonstrate a delivered fixed-position rule. Future actual DB/task IDs are unavailable.

finite structural batch shuffle without replacement
actual publisher normalization and stable identities
captured inventory and within-batch content deduplication
learner freshness, band weighting, uniform deterministic selection and unconfigured fallback rules
delivery.result: No construction rejection removes a valid sampled target: nonempty REF is constructed directly and the policy wrapper preserves valid calls. Delivery retains all five batch records and all 96 tested independent shape/target cases. Read-only selection reproduction reaches every captured or projected candidate with positive easy weight; zero easy weight and no-policy fallback tested explicitly.

limitations: Finite samples and prespecified simple strategies cannot certify the absence of all shortcuts.

Captured inventory basis 5362; concurrent publication may change duplicates. No future entity IDs, active policy snapshot or learner history supplied. Selection conclusions are conditional on examined branches; no live learner delivery is claimed.
Canonical source lacks answer-field evidence; its matrix and solution are supported, its missing original control bank cannot be reproduced.

The five stored generated questions have no captured historical generation metadata. Current content was reproduced through published stable identities with controlled seed 0; that seed is not asserted as historical.

The exact batch has singleton visible cue cells. Memorizing an item or post-hoc lookup table is possible in any finite pool; it is not treated as independent evidence of a repeated construction shortcut.
